question.knowledge_point: Proving Statements Using the Vector Space Axioms
question.problem:
From top to bottom, fill in the blanks and hence complete the proof of the following statement using the axioms $[\text{A}1]-[\text{A}8]$ given below.

*Statement: *

*$0x=0$ for any $x\in V$* 

*Proof:*

$$
\begin{aligned}0x & =0x &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (0+0)x & =0x &  & [\,\text{property of number }0\,] \\ 0x+0x & =0x &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,] \\ (0x+0x)+(-0x) & =0x+(-0x) &  & [\,\text{add }-0x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (0x+0x)+(-0x) & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ 0x+(0x+(-0x)) & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A2}\,] \\ 0x+0 & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ 0x & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom __}\,\,]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The axioms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{[A1]}:x+y=y+x & \text{[A5]}:1\cdot x=x \\ \text{[A2]}:(x+y)+z=x+(y+z) & \text{[A6]}:\alpha (\beta x)=(\alpha \beta )x \\ \text{[A3]}:x+0=x & \text{[A7]}:(\alpha +\beta )x=\alpha x+\beta x \\ \text{[A4]}:x+(-x)=0 & \text{[A8]}:\alpha (x+y)=\alpha x+\alpha y\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Using the vector space axioms, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}0x & =0x &  & [\,\text{given}\,] \\ (0+0)x & =0x &  & [\,\text{property of number }0\,] \\ 0x+0x & =0x &  & [\,\text{axiom }\text{A7}\,] \\ (0x+0x)+(-0x) & =0x+(-0x) &  & [\,\text{add }-0x\text{ to both sides}\,] \\ (0x+0x)+(-0x) & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ 0x+(0x+(-0x)) & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A2}\,] \\ 0x+0 & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom A4}\,] \\ 0x & =0 &  & [\,\text{axiom }\text{A3}\,]\end{aligned}
$$
